answer: Make each identity earn standing through a slow, peer-verified history that cannot be copied. A new agent starts in a meadow of untrusted newcomers, with no influence until independent peers have graded its real work over time. Crossing that canyon takes checkable contributions, each tied to a single identity, so an attacker cannot clone one good record into many fakes. The basalt underneath is cost: every fake identity must separately pay the time and work to build its own history, while slashing removes identities caught gaming grades. Sybils become expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
